question: How many total records are in the table?
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_count FROM table_name;

question: Show the top 5 items ordered by value descending
expected_sql: SELECT name, value FROM items ORDER BY value DESC LIMIT 5;

question: Count records grouped by category
expected_sql: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS category_count FROM items GROUP BY category ORDER BY category_count DESC;

question: Find the average price and total count for each product category
expected_sql: SELECT category, AVG(price) AS avg_price, COUNT(*) AS total_items FROM products GROUP BY category ORDER BY avg_price DESC;

question: List all orders placed in each month
expected_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS order_month, COUNT(*) AS total_orders FROM orders GROUP BY strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) ORDER BY order_month;

question: Show orders from the last 30 days
expected_sql: SELECT order_id, order_date, status FROM orders WHERE order_date >= date('now', '-30 days') ORDER BY order_date DESC;

question: Concatenate first name and last name as full name
expected_sql: SELECT first_name || ' ' || last_name AS full_name FROM employees ORDER BY full_name LIMIT 100;

question: Find the number of days between two dates
expected_sql: SELECT order_id, CAST(julianday(delivery_date) - julianday(order_date) AS INTEGER) AS days_to_deliver FROM orders WHERE delivery_date IS NOT NULL ORDER BY days_to_deliver DESC LIMIT 100;

question: Total revenue by region with join
expected_sql: SELECT c.region, SUM(o.amount) AS total_revenue FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.region ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

question: Find records that have no matching entries in another table
expected_sql: SELECT p.name, p.category FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE oi.product_id IS NULL;

question: What percentage of total sales comes from each category?
expected_sql: SELECT category, SUM(amount) AS category_total, ROUND(SUM(amount) * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(amount) FROM sales), 2) AS percentage FROM sales GROUP BY category ORDER BY percentage DESC;

question: Show yearly trends with year extraction
expected_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', created_date) AS year, COUNT(*) AS total_count FROM records GROUP BY strftime('%Y', created_date) ORDER BY year;

question: List all distinct categories for each group
expected_sql: SELECT group_id, group_concat(DISTINCT category) AS categories FROM items GROUP BY group_id;

question: Use CASE WHEN for conditional aggregation
expected_sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS total, SUM(CASE WHEN priority = 'high' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_priority_count FROM tickets GROUP BY status ORDER BY total DESC;

question: Find the top 3 sellers by number of transactions
expected_sql: SELECT seller_id, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count, SUM(amount) AS total_amount FROM transactions GROUP BY seller_id ORDER BY transaction_count DESC LIMIT 3;

question: Show null-safe filtering with COALESCE
expected_sql: SELECT name, COALESCE(description, 'No description') AS description, COALESCE(category, 'Uncategorized') AS category FROM products ORDER BY name LIMIT 100;

question: Find the running total of sales ordered by date
expected_sql: SELECT sale_date, amount, SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY sale_date) AS running_total FROM sales ORDER BY sale_date;

question: Rank items within each category by score
expected_sql: SELECT category, name, score, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY score DESC) AS rank FROM items;

question: Use a CTE to find above-average values
expected_sql: WITH avg_calc AS (SELECT AVG(salary) AS avg_salary FROM employees) SELECT e.name, e.salary FROM employees e, avg_calc WHERE e.salary > avg_calc.avg_salary ORDER BY e.salary DESC;

question: Extract quarter from date and aggregate by quarter
expected_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', order_date) AS year, CASE WHEN CAST(strftime('%m', order_date) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 1 AND 3 THEN 'Q1' WHEN CAST(strftime('%m', order_date) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 4 AND 6 THEN 'Q2' WHEN CAST(strftime('%m', order_date) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 7 AND 9 THEN 'Q3' ELSE 'Q4' END AS quarter, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY year, quarter ORDER BY year, quarter;

question: Use substr for string manipulation
expected_sql: SELECT substr(name, 1, 3) AS prefix, COUNT(*) AS count FROM items GROUP BY substr(name, 1, 3) ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 10;

question: Find customers with multiple orders using HAVING
expected_sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(total_amount) AS total_spent FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 100;

question: Multi-table join with aggregation
expected_sql: SELECT c.name AS customer, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 10;

question: Date arithmetic with SQLite modifiers
expected_sql: SELECT name, start_date, date(start_date, '+1 year') AS renewal_date FROM subscriptions WHERE date(start_date, '+1 year') <= date('now') ORDER BY start_date LIMIT 100;

question: Subquery with NOT IN for exclusion pattern
expected_sql: SELECT customer_id, name FROM customers WHERE customer_id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM orders WHERE order_date >= date('now', '-1 year')) ORDER BY name LIMIT 100;

question: What are the top product categories by number of items sold?
expected_sql: SELECT p.category, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_items_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY total_items_sold DESC LIMIT 10;

question: What are the top product categories by total sales revenue?
expected_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 10;

question: Find the top 5 teams with the highest number of wins in any single season.
expected_sql: SELECT name, year, w FROM team ORDER BY w DESC LIMIT 5;

question: Show total sales by year.
expected_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', order_date) AS sales_year, SUM(total_amount) AS total_sales FROM orders GROUP BY sales_year ORDER BY sales_year DESC;
